h1: The 7 Best Video Doorbells That Work With Mechanical Chimes of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Doorbells for Mechanical Chimes: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 video doorbells compared on wiring, power type and resolution, with notes on which suit a ding-dong chime inside your home.
summary: The Ring Wired Doorbell 2K Plus is the best video doorbell for a mechanical chime: wired power, 2K video and no battery to recharge. The Ring 4K Pro adds 4K and 10x zoom for long driveways, and the WYZE v2 is the budget wired option. Battery and PoE models are for homes where the old wiring is not usable.
intro: A mechanical chime is the box in your hall with a solenoid and two tone bars, and it rings because the old button completes a low-voltage circuit. A video doorbell must live in that same circuit if you want the ding-dong to survive the upgrade. That makes the first question how the doorbell is powered, long before anyone asks about picture sharpness.

Seven models are covered here. Most of the strong picks are wired, since tapping the existing doorbell circuit is the usual way to keep a mechanical chime. Battery and PoE models are included for homes without suitable wiring, but they come with caveats you should read first: neither of them rings the hall chime by itself, so a separate plug-in chime is likely.

products.name: Ring Wired Doorbell 2K Plus
products.verdict: Wired power, 2K video and no battery to recharge. The easiest fit for a house with a working chime.
products.description:
The Ring Wired Doorbell 2K Plus draws power from the existing doorbell circuit, records 2K video and has no battery to charge. Wiring into that circuit is what keeps the mechanical chime working, since the doorbell uses the same low-voltage line the old button did.

It ranks first because it combines the wired install, a sharp picture and the largest smart-home ecosystem. The 4K Pro adds detail for more money, and the WYZE and Blink cost less with smaller ecosystems.

Buy it for a home with a working mechanical chime. The caveats are real: it needs a compatible transformer and some wiring work, and full history needs a subscription. Skip it if you rent and cannot touch the wiring.
products.idealFor: Homes with a working mechanical chime.
products.skipIf: You rent and cannot touch the wiring.

products.name: Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro
products.verdict: 4K video and up to 10x zoom on the same wired platform. Worth it if you want detail.
products.description:
The Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro delivers 4K video with up to 10x zoom on the same wired platform. Zoom and resolution matter at distance: a face on a wide porch or long driveway is only a few pixels on a 1080p camera, while 4K keeps detail when you crop in.

It ranks second because a 2K picture already suits most porches, and it costs more than the 2K Plus. It needs the same compatible wiring.

Buy it for a long driveway or a wide porch where detail at range matters. Skip it if a 2K picture is enough. Check your transformer voltage first, since the extra processing does not change the power requirement.

products.name: WYZE Wired Doorbell Camera v2
products.verdict: Head-to-toe view, starlight night color and an accessible price for a wired 2K doorbell.
products.description:
The WYZE Wired Doorbell Camera v2 offers 2K video, head-to-toe framing, starlight color night footage and a compact body, wired to the doorbell circuit, at an accessible price. Head-to-toe framing shows packages on the step as well as visitors' faces.

It ranks third because its ecosystem is smaller than Ring's, and chime setup needs checking. It beats the Blink on the head-to-toe view.

Buy it for a budget upgrade with a wide view. Skip it if you want the broadest smart-home support. Read the manual on chime compatibility before you cut power at the breaker, and keep the old button handy in case you need to revert. Wyze's low price makes it the easiest wired model to justify when the doorbell is only a secondary camera.
products.idealFor: Budget upgrades with a wide view.
products.skipIf: You want the broadest smart-home support.

products.name: Blink Wired Doorbell 2K+
products.verdict: Connects to existing doorbell wiring and delivers 2K video inside the Amazon ecosystem.
products.description:
The Blink Wired Doorbell 2K+ connects to existing doorbell wiring, records 2K video and integrates with Amazon Alexa. Setup is simple, and it sits at the lowest price among the wired models here.

It ranks fourth because it has fewer features than Ring, and chime support needs checking. It fits Alexa homes best.

Buy it if your home runs on Alexa and the wiring is in place. Skip it if you use Google Home or Apple Home. Confirm that your chime works with it, since not every mechanical chime rings with every wired model. A cheap price helps, but a doorbell that leaves the hall chime silent has missed the point of this guide, so check before you commit.
products.idealFor: Alexa households with wiring in place.
products.skipIf: You use Google Home or Apple Home.

products.name: Ring Battery Doorbell 2K
products.verdict: Battery power means no wiring, but it will not ring a hall mechanical chime on its own.
products.description:
The Ring Battery Doorbell 2K has wide-angle 2K video, up to 6x zoom, live view and two-way talk, with no wiring required. A battery solves the install in a rental, where there is no accessible wiring.

It ranks fifth because it does not use the old chime and needs a separate one. The battery needs recharging, and it will not ring a hall mechanical chime on its own.

Buy it for a renter or a door with no wiring. Skip it if you want your hall chime to ring. For a home with a working chime, the wired Ring models give a better result.
cons: Does not use the old chime
products.idealFor: Renters and doors with no wiring.
products.skipIf: You want your hall chime to ring.

products.name: eufy Security Video Doorbell E340
products.verdict: Two cameras, one for visitors and one for the doorstep, with battery power and no wiring.
products.description:
The eufy Security Video Doorbell E340 has two cameras, one for visitors and one for the doorstep, with battery power, 2K video and no wiring. A second camera watches parcels on the ground, which a single-lens doorbell misses.

It ranks sixth because it does not trigger the old chime, and the battery needs recharging. The body is chunkier than most.

Buy it for parcel watching with no wiring. Skip it if your mechanical chime must ring. It is a good choice only where wiring is not possible, and the second camera genuinely helps with porch pirates. A plug-in chime restores the sound, though not the original hall box.
cons: Does not trigger the old chime

products.name: REOLINK Video Doorbell PoE 2K
products.verdict: A PoE doorbell with a 135-degree view, for homes with an ethernet cable at the door.
products.description:
The REOLINK Video Doorbell PoE 2K uses an ethernet cable for power and data, records 2K video with a 135 degree view and includes a wedge kit. A PoE connection is steady and has no battery or transformer to worry about.

It ranks last because it does not use the doorbell circuit and is the hardest install here. Most homes do not have ethernet at the door.

Buy it if your network already has a cable at the door. Skip it if you only have old doorbell wiring. Check the listing to see how it handles a mechanical chime before assuming the sound will carry. The wedge kit helps aim the camera down a long path, and a single ethernet run avoids battery chores entirely.
products.idealFor: PoE networks with a cable at the door.
products.skipIf: You only have old doorbell wiring.

whatMatters.detail: A mechanical chime runs on a small transformer, often 16 to 24 volts. Most wired video doorbells list a supported voltage range, and a transformer below it will not power the camera reliably. Read the transformer's label or the chime's rating and compare it with the doorbell listing before you buy, since an underpowered unit may reboot, buzz or drop offline at night.

A battery doorbell has no connection to the doorbell circuit, so it cannot ring a mechanical chime directly. You usually use a plug-in chime or the phone app. If you love the ding-dong sound, choose a wired model such as the Ring 2K Plus. The Ring Battery 2K and eufy E340 both work this way.

Some video doorbells need a small bypass or power kit installed across the chime so the circuit keeps flowing. The kit sits inside the chime box, and the listing or the manual explains whether you need one. Do not skip it, because it prevents buzzing and keeps the chime from chattering whenever the camera wakes.

2K is plenty for a small porch. 4K and 10x zoom help on wide porches and long driveways, where a face is far from the lens. Pick resolution based on the distance, not on the box number alone. The Ring 4K Pro suits long approaches, while the 2K Plus covers most front doors.

Live view is often free, but saved clips and history usually need a monthly plan. Check which features are free on the listing, and decide whether you want cloud storage before you choose a brand. Ring lists a subscription for full history, so factor it into the cost over a few years, and compare it with local storage options.

faq.q: Will a video doorbell ring my existing chime?
faq.a: Wired models that connect to your doorbell circuit usually can. Battery models generally cannot. Check each listing and confirm your transformer voltage first, since the Ring 2K Plus and WYZE v2 need a compatible one.

faq.q: Do I need a bypass kit?
faq.a: Some wired doorbells need a small power kit installed across the chime to prevent buzzing or loss of power. The listing and manual say whether yours is required, so read them before you start the install.

faq.q: Can I use a battery doorbell with a mechanical chime?
faq.a: Not directly. A battery doorbell is not connected to the doorbell circuit, so you would use a separate plug-in chime. The Ring Battery 2K and eufy E340 follow this model, and neither rings the hall box.

faq.q: Is the Ring Wired 4K Pro worth it over the 2K Plus?
faq.a: If you want to see detail at a distance, yes. The 4K Pro has 4K video and up to 10x zoom. For ordinary porches, the 2K Plus is enough and costs less.

Many wired doorbells list a supported range, often 16 to 24 volts AC. Read the label on your transformer or chime and compare it with the doorbell listing, and ask an electrician if the numbers do not match.

faq.q: Does PoE work with a mechanical chime?
faq.a: PoE uses an ethernet cable rather than the doorbell circuit, so check the listing before assuming it will ring a mechanical chime. The Reolink PoE model is the one for homes with ethernet at the door.

finalTake: The Ring Wired Doorbell 2K Plus is the right video doorbell for a home with a working mechanical chime, because it uses the existing circuit and avoids batteries. Choose the 4K Pro for long driveways and the WYZE v2 for budget. Pick battery or PoE only when the old wiring is not an option.
